title: Birth Defects Registry Coordinator - Public Health

cond_0001.intro:
The Birth Defects Registry Coordinator is the primary implementer of the [Location masked] Birth Defects Registry. The Coordinator provides training and technical assistance to laboratory facilities, hospitals, and clinics across the state to ensure proper identification and reporting of birth defects in [Location masked]'s children with the goal of helping them live better and healthier lives.
The Coordinator is tasked with developing and implementing data quality efforts so that birth defects are properly enumerated and reported to the agency, providers, federal partners and the public.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Implementation and development of scientific investigations and research concerning the causes, methods of prevention, treatment and cure of birth defects through collaboration with epidemiology teammates and clinical partners.
Representing [Location masked] through presentations at national meetings, workgroup conference calls, grand rounds, and advisory committee meetings.
Serving as a subject matter expert for internal programmatic planning.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Statistics, Health Education, or Nursing with substantial experience in the analysis, interpretation, and management of epidemiological data related to a specific disease or health subject area.
Bachelor's degree in Statistics or related field plus three years of experience in statistics, data collection, data management, or a related area.
Preferred Requirements
Master's degree in Statistics or related field and one year of experience in statistics, data collection, data management, or a related area.
Knowledge of the causes, methods of prevention, treatment and cure of birth defects; public health surveillance; and data quality and governance.
Clinical experience or history of working with clinical data.
Ability to work evening hours, infrequently, to provide training to reporting facilities.

The Coordinator provides training and technical assistance to laboratory facilities, hospitals, and clinics across the state to ensure proper identification and reporting of birth defects in [Location masked]'s children with the goal of helping them live better and healthier lives.
The Coordinator is tasked with developing and implementing data quality efforts so that birth defects are properly enumerated and reported to the agency, providers, federal partners and the public.
cond_0055.responsibilities:
Implementation and development of scientific investigations and research concerning the causes, methods of prevention, treatment and cure of birth defects through collaboration with epidemiology teammates and clinical partners.
Representing [Location masked] through presentations at national meetings, workgroup conference calls, grand rounds, and advisory committee meetings.
Serving as a subject matter expert for internal programmatic planning.
cond_0055.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Statistics, Health Education, or Nursing with substantial experience in the analysis, interpretation, and management of epidemiological data related to a specific disease or health subject area.
Bachelor's degree in Statistics or related field plus three years of experience in statistics, data collection, data management, or a related area.
Preferred Requirements
Master's degree in Statistics or related field and one year of experience in statistics, data collection, data management, or a related area.
Knowledge of the causes, methods of prevention, treatment and cure of birth defects; public health surveillance; and data quality and governance.
Clinical experience or history of working with clinical data.
Ability to work evening hours, infrequently, to provide training to reporting facilities.

The Coordinator is tasked with developing and implementing data quality efforts so that birth defects are properly enumerated and reported to the agency, providers, federal partners and the public. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of public health surveillance and epidemiological data work.
cond_0193.responsibilities:
The implementation and development of scientific investigations and research concerning the causes, methods of prevention, treatment and cure of birth defects through collaboration with epidemiology teammates and clinical partners.
Representing [Location masked] through presentations at national meetings, workgroup conferences calls, grand rounds, advisory committee meetings.
Serving as a subject matter expert for internal programmatic planning.
cond_0193.requirements:
Master's degree in Statistics or related field and one year experience in statistics, data collection, data management or related area OR Bachelor's degree in Statistics or related field plus three years experience in any of the above or related area.
Bachelor's Degree in Public Health, Statistics, or Health Education, or Nursing coupled with substantial experience spanning multiple years in the analysis, interpretation, and management of epidemiological data related to the specific disease or health subject area.
Knowledge of the causes, methods of prevention, treatment and cure of birth defects; public health surveillance; and data quality and governance.
Clinical experience or history of working with clinical data.
Ability to work evening hours, infrequently, to provide training to reporting facilities.
cond_0193.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

The Coordinator provides training and technical assistance to laboratory facilities, hospitals, and clinics across the state to ensure proper identification and reporting of birth defects in [Location masked]'s children with the goal of helping them live better and healthier lives.
The Coordinator is tasked with developing and implementing data quality efforts so that birth defects are properly enumerated and reported to the agency, providers, federal partners and the public.
cond_0281.responsibilities:
The Coordinator is also tasked with:
The implementation and development of scientific investigations and research concerning the causes, methods of prevention, treatment and cure of birth defects through collaboration with epidemiology teammates and clinical partners. Representing [Location masked] through presentations at national meetings, workgroup conferences calls, grand rounds, advisory committee meetings. Serving as a subject matter expert for internal programmatic planning.
cond_0281.requirements:
Master's degree in Statistics or related field and demonstrated expertise in statistics, data collection, data management or related area; OR Bachelor's degree in Statistics or related field plus substantial experience (minimum three years) in any of the above or related area.
Bachelor's Degree in Public Health, Statistics, Health Education, or Nursing coupled with significant, proven experience across multiple years in the analysis, interpretation, and management of epidemiological data related to the specific disease or health subject area.
Advanced knowledge of the causes, methods of prevention, treatment and cure of birth defects; public health surveillance; and data quality and governance.
Proven track record of clinical experience or working extensively with clinical data.
Ability to work evening hours, infrequently, to provide training to reporting facilities.

The Coordinator provides training and technical assistance to laboratory facilities, hospitals, and clinics across the state to ensure proper identification and reporting of birth defects in [Location masked]'s children with the goal of helping them live better and healthier lives.
The Coordinator is tasked with developing and implementing data quality efforts so that birth defects are properly enumerated and reported to the agency, providers, federal partners and the public.
cond_0372.responsibilities:
The Coordinator is also tasked with:
The implementation and development of scientific investigations and research concerning the causes, methods of prevention, treatment and cure of birth defects through collaboration with epidemiology teammates and clinical partners. Representing [Location masked] through presentations at national meetings, workgroup conferences calls, grand rounds, advisory committee meetings. Serving as a subject matter expert for internal programmatic planning.
cond_0372.requirements:
Around one year of experience in statistics, data collection, data management, or a related area, combined with a Master's degree in Statistics or related field; or around three years of experience in any of the above or related area combined with a Bachelor's degree in Statistics or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
A Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Statistics, Health Education, or Nursing, or equivalent practical experience, along with substantial experience in the analysis, interpretation, and management of epidemiological data related to a specific disease or health subject area.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
Background in the causes, methods of prevention, treatment and cure of birth defects; public health surveillance; and data quality and governance. Some clinical experience or familiarity with clinical data is helpful.
Skills: Some clinical experience or history of working with clinical data.
Ability to work evening hours, infrequently, to provide training to reporting facilities.

The Birth Defects Registry Coordinator is the primary implementer of the [Location masked] Birth Defects Registry. Working alongside laboratory facilities, hospitals, and clinics across the state, the Coordinator helps ensure proper identification and reporting of birth defects in [Location masked]'s children with the goal of supporting better and healthier lives.

Represent [Location masked] through presentations at national meetings, workgroup conference calls, grand rounds, and advisory committee meetings.
Serve as a subject matter expert for internal programmatic planning, sharing knowledge and supporting colleagues across the program.
cond_0513.requirements:

Master's degree in Statistics or related field and one year of experience in statistics, data collection, data management, or related area; OR Bachelor's degree in Statistics or related field plus three years of experience in any of the above or related area.
Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Statistics, Health Education, or Nursing coupled with substantial experience in the analysis, interpretation, and management of epidemiological data related to the specific disease or health subject area.
Preferred Requirements
Knowledge of the causes, methods of prevention, treatment, and cure of birth defects; public health surveillance; and data quality and governance.
Clinical experience or history of working with clinical data.
Ability to work evening hours, infrequently, to provide training to reporting facilities.

Working alongside laboratory facilities, hospitals, and clinics across the state, the Coordinator helps ensure proper identification and reporting of birth defects in [Location masked]'s children with the goal of supporting better and healthier lives.
The Coordinator works with the agency to develop and support data quality efforts so that birth defects are properly enumerated and reported to the agency, providers, federal partners, and the public.
cond_0531.responsibilities:
Work with epidemiology teammates and clinical partners to support the implementation and development of scientific investigations and research concerning the causes, methods of prevention, treatment, and cure of birth defects.
Provide training and technical assistance to reporting facilities, coordinating with laboratory facilities, hospitals, and clinics to support proper identification and reporting.
Represent [Location masked] through presentations at national meetings, workgroup conference calls, grand rounds, and advisory committee meetings.
Serve as a subject matter expert for internal programmatic planning, sharing knowledge and supporting colleagues across the program.
cond_0531.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Master's degree in Statistics or related field and one year of experience in statistics, data collection, data management, or related area; OR Bachelor's degree in Statistics or related field plus three years of experience in any of the above or related area.
Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Statistics, Health Education, or Nursing coupled with substantial experience in the analysis, interpretation, and management of epidemiological data related to the specific disease or health subject area.
Preferred Requirements
Knowledge of the causes, methods of prevention, treatment, and cure of birth defects; public health surveillance; and data quality and governance.
Clinical experience or history of working with clinical data.
Ability to work evening hours, infrequently, to provide training to reporting facilities.
